title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference Guide, Day‑2 Ops, and Customer Requirements
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Overview

This document consolidates best practices, reference architectures, and operational playbooks for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on\u2011prem). It is intended for SREs, Platform Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and customer technical contacts responsible for installation, day\u20112 operations, and upgrades.

Goals
- Provide a repeatable, secure VPC and on\u2011prem deployment pattern for Redwood Private.
- Define day\u20112 operational procedures (monitoring, backups, incident response).
- Document upgrade and rollback steps with clear safety gates.
- Capture a customer requirements library for pre\u2011sales and onboarding readiness checks.

Scope
- VPC deployments (AWS, GCP, Azure) using customer VPC with private subnets and service endpoints.
- On\u2011prem packaging options (air\u2011gapped bundles, host requirements, installer tooling).
- Day\u20112 operational playbook (capacity, observability, troubleshooting).
- Upgrade & rollback playbook for minor and major releases.
- Customer requirements checklist and sizing guidance.

1) Reference Architectures

1.1 VPC (recommended for most enterprise customers)
- Components: control plane (Redwood managed or customer-hosted), Private data plane (in-customer VPC), ingress gateway, load balancer, NAT/egress gateways, KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- Network segmentation: management, inference, storage tiers in separate subnets; restrict egress with egress-only NAT and security groups.
- High availability: multi-AZ placement for inference nodes, control-plane endpoints across AZs where supported.

Diagram (text):
- Customer VPC: public subnets (bastion, ops), private subnets (inference nodes), DB subnets (if DB required), S3/NFS endpoints.
- Redwood Private control plane communicates to data plane over mutually authenticated mTLS; customers may require a VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud.

1.2 On\u2011Prem Reference (air\u2011gapped option)
- Use cases: regulated environments, strict data residency, offline clusters.
- Packaging: OCI tarball of runtime images + offline installer, signed manifests, checksum file.
- Storage: recommend POSIX-compatible NFS or Ceph; object-store compatibility layer required for S3 semantics.
- Hardware: see Customer Requirements table below for minimum CPU/GPU/Network guidance.

2) On\u2011Prem Packaging & Installer

Installer variants:
- Online (container registry access): Helm + operator manifests, RBAC, and CRDs.
- Offline (air\u2011gapped): bundle.tar.gz with images, Helm chart, certificate CA bundle, and installation script.

Installation checklist (high level):
1. Validate host prerequisites (OS, kernel, required kernel modules).
2. Provision storage volumes and mount points.
3. Load offline images (if air\u2011gapped) into local registry and update Helm values to point to local registry.
4. Apply Helm chart with tuned resource requests/limits per sizing profile.
5. Run smoke tests (health endpoints, sample inference).

CLI snippets (example):
- Helm install: helm upgrade --install redwood-private redwood/redwood-private -f customer-values.yaml --namespace redwood
- Offline image load (example): ctr images import images-bundle.tar.gz && kubectl apply -f local-registry-secret.yaml

3) Day\u20112 Operations (Runbook)

3.1 Monitoring and Alerts
- Metrics to monitor (minimum): inference_latency_p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, kv_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_utilization, node_memory_utilization, pod_restart_count, disk_iops, control_plane_heartbeat.
- Recommended alert thresholds (examples):
  - inference_p99_latency > 1500ms for 5m -> P1 page (owner: infra-sre).
  - gpu_utilization > 95% for 10m -> P2 (owner: platform).
  - pod_restart_count > 3 in 15m -> P3 (owner: owning-service).
- Audit logs: forward API request and invocation logs to customer SIEM (retain per contract).

3.2 Backups & Disaster Recovery
- Control plane state: nightly backup to encrypted customer object store or S3-compatible endpoint.
- Model artifacts & storage: snapshot models and checkpoint metadata daily (policy configurable).
- Restore exercises: run quarterly DR test that restores control-plane DB to a staging environment and validates boot.

3.3 Capacity Management
- Autoscaling: recommend HPA/VPA or custom autoscaler tied to tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
- Capacity plan: maintain 20% buffer above steady-state peak for burst tolerance; maintain a reserve pool for cold-starts.

3.4 Common Troubleshooting Steps (ordered)
1. Check control-plane health: kubectl get pods -n redwood; control-plane-api should be Ready.
2. Verify data-plane connectivity: curl -kv https://inference.internal.health/healthz with mTLS cert.
3. Inspect model server logs: kubectl logs deployment/model-server -n redwood | tail -n 500.
4. Check GPU drivers and node readiness: nvidia-smi; kubectl describe node <node> for taints/conditions.

4) Upgrade & Rollback Procedures

4.1 Pre\u2011upgrade gates (must pass before starting)
- All critical alerts cleared for 24h.
- Snapshot of control-plane DB taken and verified.
- Canary deployment plan with 5\u201310% of traffic routed to new version.
- Automated E2E smoke tests passing in staging.

4.2 Minor version upgrade (patch/minor) \u2013 safe path
1. Create release branch and upload new images to registry.
2. Update Helm chart values with new image tags and change-log.
3. Deploy to staging and run smoke + perf tests.
4. Roll forward to canary (5% traffic) and monitor key metrics for 30 minutes.
5. If metrics stable, increment canary to 25% for 60 minutes, then 100% with monitoring.

4.3 Major upgrade (breaking changes) \u2013 recommended controlled rollout
- Require engineering release manager and at least two approvers.
- Schedule maintenance window and notify customer stakeholders.
- Run database migrations in a separate, transactional job with rollback scripts prepared.

4.4 Rollback plan (if metrics breach or failure)
- Procedure: revert Helm release to previous revision: helm rollback redwood-private <REVISION> --namespace redwood.
- Restore control-plane DB snapshot if schema changes were applied and rollback requires DB restore.
- Run validation suite and confirm throughput/latency are restored.

Safety checklist (post\u2011rollback): verify no tombstoned resources, rehydrate caches, and notify stakeholders.

5) Customer Requirements Library (pre\u2011sales & onboarding checklist)

Table: Minimum and Recommended Requirements
| Area | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| CPU (control plane) | 8 vCPU | 16 vCPU | Depends on number of concurrent deployments |
| GPU (inference) | 1xA10 / 1xA100 per 8 concurrent large requests | pool of 4xA100 | For most production workloads, use >=4 GPUs per cluster |
| RAM (per inference node) | 32 GB | 128 GB | Large context models require more host RAM |
| Disk | 500 GB SSD | 2 TB NVMe | Low-latency disk recommended for KV cache |
| Network | 1 Gbps | 10 Gbps | Recommend 10 Gbps for multi-GPU clusters |
| Storage | POSIX NFS or S3-compatible | Ceph or S3 with versioning | Object store for model artifacts |

Onboarding checklist (customer-facing)
- Provide cloud account IDs and admin contact.
- VPC diagram and CIDR blocks for management and data plane.
- KMS/HSM details and access procedure for envelope encryption.
- Network ACLs, approved outbound endpoints, and proxy details (if present).
- Compliance requirements (e.g., SOC2, HIPAA) and required confidentiality labels.

6) Ownership & SLAs
- Core owners: Platform Engineering (primary), Infra SRE (oncall), Solutions Eng (onboarding).
- Typical SLA targets for private deployments (negotiable at contract time):
  - Control plane API: 99.9% monthly uptime.
  - Inference 95th percentile latency target: customer-specific, baseline 150ms for short prompts.

7) Appendices
A. Example Helm values (snippet)
replicaCount: 3
image:
  registry: "registry.internal.example.com/redwood"
  tag: "v2026.01.2"
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "2000m"
    memory: "8Gi"
  limits:
    cpu: "4000m"
    memory: "16Gi"
nodeSelector:
  workload: inference

B. Contact Matrix
- Release manager: eng-release@redwood.example.com
- SRE oncall: pager duty link (internal)
- Solutions Eng: solutions-eng@redwood.example.com

C. Change log & references
- See related pages: private-deployments-playbook-2026 (operational playbook), private-deployments-reference-architectures-2026 (detailed diagrams).

Document governance: Reviewed quarterly by Platform Engineering and updated as new runtime features (quantization profiles, batching policies) ship.

End of document.
